issues.description: Method signature mismatch for Farm.singFarmSongVerse: the UML in the problem statement declares a private helper singFarmSongVerse that accepts an Animal parameter (singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal)). In the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) the method is present but the Animal parameter is commented out (private void singFarmSong(/*Animal animal*/) { ... }). The reference solution (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java) implements private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }. This inconsistency between the template and the UML/solution can confuse students about the intended helper API and makes it non-obvious how to implement singFarmSong() to iterate over animals and call the helper.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template helper signature match the UML/solution by changing the template declaration to accept an Animal parameter (e.g. private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... }) and update its body accordingly. Alternatively, if the parameterless helper was intentional, update the UML/problem statement to reflect the parameterless variant. Prefer aligning the template with the UML/solution so students can implement singFarmSong() by iterating animals and calling singFarmSongVerse(animal).

issues.description: Class-name divergence for the Animal subclasses: the problem statement UML and the template example (Main.java) refer to concrete classes named Seal, Pig, and Goat. The provided reference implementation instead supplies classes named SpaceSeal, SpacePig, and SpaceGoat (with non-empty implementations) while the expected names Seal.java, Pig.java, and Goat.java in the solution are empty. This naming mismatch between the exercise description/template and the reference solution can confuse students and automated checks that expect the exact class names Seal, Pig, and Goat.
issues.suggestedFix: Align class names across artifacts. Either rename the reference classes to the expected names (SpaceSeal -> Seal, SpacePig -> Pig, SpaceGoat -> Goat) or add thin adapter/alias classes with the expected names that extend/delegate to the Space* implementations (for example, class Seal extends SpaceSeal { public Seal(String name){super(name);} }). Alternatively, update the problem statement and template to explicitly document the Space* naming if that naming is intentional. Ensure the chosen fix preserves the exercise API expected by tests and students.
